title: Forward block restriction in symmetric active slices
statement: Use symmetric operadic families and active and inert edges of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], join slices of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], and the cocartesian mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. Let $n\geq1$ and let $M^\otimes\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^n$ be a small symmetric operadic family. Write $M_0^\otimes$ for its parameter-zero fiber and define its active incoming slices $J_b=M_0^\otimes\times_{M^\otimes}(M^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})_{/b}$. Let $b$ have positive coordinate and lie over $\langle s\rangle$, let $a:x\to b$ with $x\in M_0^\otimes$ be active with pointed map $\alpha:\langle k\rangle\to\langle s\rangle$, and choose inert projections $b\to b_j$. Put $D_j=\alpha^{-1}(j)$, and lift the inert maps $\langle k\rangle\to(D_j)_+$ at $x$ to $p_j:x\to x_j$ in $M_0^\otimes$. Then composition with $b\to b_j$ and inert-active factorization gives active arrows $a_j:x_j\to b_j$ and, on coherent triangles and all higher simplices, a natural functor $P:J_b\to\prod_{j=1}^sJ_{b_j}$ sending $(a,h)$ to $(a_j,h_j)$, where the induced block triangles $h_j$, together with their comparison homotopies, are determined up to a contractible space of coherent choices. This includes empty input blocks and $s=0$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336-337; relative cocartesian factorization and blockwise Segal comparison.

proof.text: Write $C_c=M_0^\otimes\times_{M^\otimes}M^\otimes_{/c}$, allowing arbitrary incoming arrows. The fiber $M_0^\otimes$ is a replete full subcategory of $M^\otimes$: a simplex of $\Delta^n$ all of whose vertices are $0$ is constant, and equivalences in $\Delta^n$ are identities. Thus $C_c$ is the full subcategory of the join slice on sources in $M_0^\otimes$, and is a small quasicategory. For calculations use its equivalent fixed-target arrow model from [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence], over the source category. The cone mapping-space formula of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] identifies a map from $u:x\to c$ to $v:z\to c$ with $h:x\to z$ in $M_0^\otimes$ and a specified triangle $vh\simeq u$, retaining its homotopies. The active objects form a full subcategory: if $u,v$ are active and $vh\simeq u$, their pointed maps satisfy $\alpha=\beta\delta$; $\delta(t)=*$ for $t\ne *$ would imply $\alpha(t)=*$, a contradiction. Therefore $h$ is active, and this full subcategory is exactly $J_c$, on every simplex.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3, proof step (1), printed pp.336-337: forward direction of the output-product comparison; agent expansion of the omitted slice factorization argument.

proof.text: Fix the chosen inert output arrow $t_j:b\to b_j$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-slice-sections] to $\mathcal C=M^\otimes$, the replete full subcategory $D=M_0^\otimes$, and the diagram $t_j:\Delta^1\to M^\otimes$. Smallness supplies its local-smallness and universe requirements. Its cocartesian slice transport gives a coherent postcomposition functor $Q_j:C_b\to C_{b_j}$, taking $a$ to $c_j=t_ja$ and a triangle $a'h\simeq a$ to $t_ja'h\simeq t_ja$. This is transport of entire coherent slice diagrams, so includes their comparison homotopies. The source projections are unchanged. The join-slice/arrow equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence] identifies this construction with the join slices in the statement.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3, proof step (1), printed pp.336-337: forward direction of the output-product comparison; agent expansion of the omitted slice factorization argument.

proof.text: For an active $\alpha:\langle k\rangle\to\langle s\rangle$ let $D_j=\alpha^{-1}(j)$. Define $\rho_{D_j}:\langle k\rangle\to(D_j)_+$ to retain $D_j$ and send its complement to $*$. It is inert. The composite $\rho_j\alpha$ factors as $\gamma_j\rho_{D_j}$, where $\gamma_j:(D_j)_+\to\langle1\rangle$ sends every element of $D_j$ to $1$. It is active even when $D_j=\varnothing$. These are literal equalities of pointed maps. For a triangle $a'h\simeq a$ let $\delta$ be the pointed map of $h$; then $\alpha=\alpha'\delta$ implies $\delta(D_j)\subseteq D'_j$ and gives an active restriction $\delta_j:(D_j)_+\to(D'_j)_+$ satisfying $\delta_j\rho_{D_j}=\rho_{D'_j}\delta$.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3, proof step (1), printed pp.336-337: forward direction of the output-product comparison; agent expansion of the omitted slice factorization argument.

proof.text: For any $c:x\to b_j$ in $C_{b_j}$, the family factorization theorem [lem-coef-symmetric-family-inert-active-orthogonality] supplies $x\xrightarrow{p}x_D\xrightarrow{r(c)}b_j$, with $p$ stationary inert, $r(c)$ active, and a composition triangle. Stationarity puts $x_D$ in $M_0^\otimes$, so $r(c)\in J_{b_j}$. For $c=c_j$ of step 2, the retained set is exactly $D_j$ of step 3. The particular inert lift $p_j$ chosen in the question may be used: apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to this $\pi$-cocartesian edge and $z=b_j$. The base factorization $(\gamma_j,0\to t)\circ(\rho_{D_j},1_0)$ and the point $c_j$ determine a point of the homotopy pullback. Its homotopy fiber is contractible; it consists of the required $a_j:x_j\to b_j$ over $(\gamma_j,0\to t)$ with its triangle $a_jp_j\simeq c_j$. Hence $a_j$ is active. The criterion applies because the family's categorical fibration is an inner fibration between quasicategories; it does not require lifts of all other base edges.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3, proof step (1), printed pp.336-337: forward direction of the output-product comparison; agent expansion of the omitted slice factorization argument.

proof.text:
The triangle in step 4 gives a universal arrow $c\to i_jr(c)$ for the full inclusion $i_j:J_{b_j}\hookrightarrow C_{b_j}$. To verify this, take an arbitrary $q:z\to b_j$ in $J_{b_j}$. The orthogonality statement of [lem-coef-symmetric-family-inert-active-orthogonality], applied to the stationary inert $p:x\to x_D$ and active $q$, gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{M^\otimes}(x_D,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{M^\otimes}(x,z)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{M^\otimes}(x,b_j)}\operatorname{Map}_{M^\otimes}(x_D,b_j).$$
Take its homotopy fiber over $r(c)$ in the last factor. On the left this is the space of triangles $qh\simeq r(c)$; on the right it is the space of triangles $qv\simeq c$, using the specified triangle $r(c)p\simeq c$. By the slice mapping formula in step 1 these are $\operatorname{Map}_{J_{b_j}}(r(c),q)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{C_{b_j}}(c,i_jq)$. Sources and targets here lie in the full $M_0^\otimes$, so the source mapping spaces are unchanged by restricting to that fiber. The comparison is precisely precomposition with the unit triangle, and is natural in $q$.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3, proof step (1), printed pp.336-337: forward direction of the output-product comparison; agent expansion of the omitted slice factorization argument.

proof.text: Apply the opposite (partial left adjoint) assertion of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $T=i_j$, with its whole target $C_{b_j}$ as the allowed full subcategory. Step 5 verifies its universal-arrow hypothesis for every object, without assuming functorial factorization in advance. We obtain a coherent reflector $R_j:C_{b_j}\to J_{b_j}$ and coherent unit $1\to i_jR_j$; the space of universal-arrow choices is contractible. Its diagram clause holds for every $K$, and commutes with every $K'\to K$. Thus $P_j=R_jQ_j|_{J_b}$ is a coherent functor, and its unit triangles give the comparison with $t_ja$. Each prescribed $p_j$ and its factorization from step 4 is a universal-arrow presentation by step 5, and consequently is identified with this one through the same contractible space of choices. This identifies the object value with $a_j$ with its comparison triangle, rather than merely identifying its class in the homotopy category.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3, proof step (1), printed pp.336-337: forward direction of the output-product comparison; agent expansion of the omitted slice factorization argument.

proof.text: Explicitly, a slice edge $h:(a:x\to b)\to(a':x'\to b)$ supplies the square with left edge $p_j:x\to x_j$, right edge $a'_j:x'_j\to b_j$, top edge $p'_jh:x\to x'_j$, and bottom edge $a_j:x_j\to b_j$. Its commutation homotopy is the composite of $a'_jp'_j\simeq t_ja'$, $a'h\simeq a$, and $t_ja\simeq a_jp_j$, including the composition homotopies of $Q_j$. Orthogonality gives the contractible space of fillers $h_j:x_j\to x'_j$ with both triangles $h_jp_j\simeq p'_jh$ and $a'_jh_j\simeq a_j$. In the pointed-set base these force the block map $\delta_j$ of step 3, so $h_j$ is active and stationary. The coherent unit from step 6 supplies these fillers simultaneously. Its diagram mapping-space equivalence, applied for $K=\Delta^r$ and restricted along faces and degeneracies, retains all their higher compatibilities. It therefore proves that these fillers are the morphisms and higher simplices of $P_j$, without an independent choice of a filler for each triangle.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3, proof step (1), printed pp.336-337: forward direction of the output-product comparison; agent expansion of the omitted slice factorization argument.

proof.text: Take $P=(P_1,\ldots,P_s)$, defined degreewise by these coherent functors; restriction in every simplicial degree acts componentwise. This is the required functor to $\prod_jJ_{b_j}$, with the block triangles of step 7 and their contractible coherent choices of step 6. No step required a nonempty $D_j$: at $D_j=\varnothing$ the inert map is $\langle k\rangle\to\langle0\rangle$, the active factor is the nullary map $\langle0\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$, and the same arguments apply. If $s=0$ there are no $j$ to choose and $P$ is the unique map to the empty product $\Delta^0$. An active arrow to $\langle0\rangle$ must have $k=0$; this is consistent with the construction and imposes no nonemptiness claim on $J_b$.
